nodes.name: IF Pretreatment
nodes.procedure: The 0.8 cm × 0.8 cm × 0.01 cm iron foam (IF) was ultrasonically cleaned with 3 M HCl, anhydrous ethanol and deionized water for 30 min successively to remove the inert oxide film on the surface. After cleaning, place it in an oven at 60 °C to dry to obtain a prefabricated foam nickel base.
nodes.source_text: The 0.8 cm × 0.8 cm × 0.01 cm iron foam (IF) was ultrasonically cleaned with 3 M HCl... oven at 60 °C to dry

nodes.name: NiFeOOH Deposition
nodes.procedure: Using an electronic balance to precisely weigh out 1 g of nickel chloride hexahydrate and dissolve it in 10 ml of deionized water. Place the pretreated IF into the prepared nickel chloride solution, and then heat the mixture in an 80 °C water bath for 1 h. Following this, remove the electrode and wash it with deionized water, dry the residue, and obtain the nickeliron hydroxide catalyst, named NiFeOOH/IF.

nodes.name: Ni Electrodeposition on NiFeOOH/IF
nodes.procedure: Using an electronic balance to accurately weigh out 2 g of nickel sulfate hexahydrate and 0.3 g of boric acid, and dissolve them in 30 ml of deionized water to obtain the electroplating solution. Next, use the prepared NiFeOOH/IF as the cathode and a platinum plate as the anode, electrodeposit for 10 min at a current of 50 mA in the prepared electroplating solution to obtain the nickel-coated nickeliron hydroxide catalyst, named Ni@NiFeOOH/IF.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni@NiFeOOH/IF possesses a three-dimensional blocky structure overlaid with a dense layer of nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figs. 1.a-b display that Ni@NiFeOOH/IF possesses a threedimensional blocky structure overlaid with a dense layer of nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni@NiFeOOH/IF consists of stacked blocks with clear nanosheet edges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As seen in Fig. 1.c, the structure consists of stacked blocks with clear nanosheet edges, in agreement with the SEM findings.

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice spacing from FFT analysis confirms NiFeOOH phase (PDF#14-0556) and Ni (111) crystal plane (PDF#89-7128), verifying the electrochemically deposited nickel layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice spacing obtained from Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis, when compared with the Powder Diffraction File (PDF) cards ((Fe0.67Ni0.33)OOH PDF#14–0556, Ni PDF#89–7128), confirms the presence of the NiFeOOH phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, and O elements across Ni@NiFeOOH/IF with Ni content notably higher than Fe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the EDX element mapping tests depicted in Figs. 2. a-d, a uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, and O elements across the material is evident, with the Ni content notably higher than that of Fe.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe signal peaks prominent on surface of Ni@NiFeOOH/IF and NiFeOOH/IF due to strong signal from IF substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3.a shows that the Fe signal peaks on the surface of Ni@NiFeOOH/IF and NiFeOOH/IF are quite prominent, which is due to the strong signal from the IF substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni@NiFeOOH/IF exhibits characteristic peaks at 670 cm^-1 (Fe-O-Fe vibration of FeOOH) and 550 cm^-1 (Ni^3+-O stretching vibration of NiOOH), confirming NiFeOOH heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Raman spectroscopy test shown in Fig. 3.b, the Ni@NiFeOOH/IF sample exhibits distinct characteristic peaks at 670 cm^-1 and 550 cm^-1, which correspond to the Fe-O-Fe vibration of FeOOH and the Ni^3+-O stretching vibration of NiOOH, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni@NiFeOOH/IF shows Ni 2p peaks for Ni^0 (852.27 eV, 869.33 eV), Ni^2+ (856.17 eV, 873.87 eV), Ni^3+ (857.76 eV, 875.6 eV) with shift to higher binding energy; Fe 2p shows Fe^0 (706.05 eV), Fe^2+ (710.74 eV, 723.2 eV), Fe^3+ (713.05 eV, 725.97 eV) also shifted; O 1s shows abundant lattice oxygen.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ni 2p spectrum shown in Fig. 3.d, the characteristic peaks at 852.27 eV and 869.33 eV can be attributed to Ni^0 ... In the Fe 2p spectrum depicted in Fig. 3.e, the peak at 706.05 eV is attributed to Fe^0 ... In the O 1s spectrum shown in Fig. 3.f, it can be observed that Ni@NiFeOOH/IF has a relatively abundant lattice oxygen.
